name: Ziba
title: Saul's Servant and Mephibosheth's Steward
summary: Ziba (also known as Siba) was a servant in Saul's household who was summoned by King David to help him find survivors from Saul's family. He was appointed to manage Mephibosheth's estates, but later falsely accused his master before David during Absalom's rebellion to secure the properties for himself.

keyEvents.title: David Finds Ziba
keyEvents.description: King David summoned Ziba, a servant from Saul's household, to ask if anyone remained of Saul's family whom he could show kindness to for Jonathan's sake.

keyEvents.title: Ziba Is Appointed to Serve Mephibosheth
keyEvents.description: David commanded Ziba, along with his sons and servants, to farm the land for Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, who was brought to eat at David's table.

keyEvents.title: Ziba Meets David During Flight from Absalom
keyEvents.description: When David fled from Absalom, Ziba met him with donkeys loaded with bread, raisin cakes, fruit, and wine. He told David that Mephibosheth had stayed in Jerusalem because he hoped to regain Saul's kingdom.

keyEvents.title: David gives Ziba the property of Mephibosheth
keyEvents.description: Based on Ziba's accusations, David gave him all of Mephibosheth's property. Ziba responded with gratitude and stated that he hoped to find favor in David's eyes.

keyEvents.title: Mephibosheth defends himself after Absalom's fall
keyEvents.description: When David returned to Jerusalem following Absalom's defeat, Mephibosheth met him and explained that Ziba had deceived and abandoned him by not preparing a donkey for him so he could follow the king.

keyEvents.title: David divides the property between Ziba and Mephibosheth
keyEvents.description: David decided that Mephibosheth and Ziba should share the land holdings, a decision that may suggest David was not entirely sure who spoke the truth.
